dialog.body: Public Works, Denise speaking, how can I help you this morning?

Hey, yeah, good morning. My name's Doug Gifford, I'm calling about the drain at 688 Thames Street, down the Fifth Ward, by the corner there. I called about this back in January and, uh, here we are again.
688 Thames. Okay, hang on, that's ringing a bell. Did somebody just call about that? I literally just got off with a Luis Morales.

Yeah, that's Ileana's son. I rent the in-law unit over the garage. He texted me he called, but I wanted to call too, 'cause honestly I'm the one who called the first time and I feel like it didn't go nowhere.
Okay. I've got it all up in front of me. Go ahead.

So the basement flooded after that big storm in January, the one that started as snow and went to rain, overnight into that Monday. About three inches. Camping gear, the chest freezer, all that got wet. I called that Wednesday, they said a crew would come Friday, and a crew did come. But all they did was clean off the top of the grate and shovel the gunk out around it. That's it. Fifteen minutes, gone. And then the rain Friday and Saturday, three days ago, it flooded again. Five inches this time. That's the second time this winter. Second time. And it's the same corner, same drain, nothing changed.
I hear you. I see the January call, I see the crew visit on the thirtieth, grate and basin top cleaned out. And Luis's report from a few minutes ago, five inches, Friday into Saturday.

Right. So, like, no offense to whoever came out, but cleaning the top of it obviously didn't fix nothing. Somethin's wrong under there. I want somebody higher up to actually look at it. Not just another truck that pulls up and scoops leaves.
That's fair. So here's where it stands as of the call I just took. There's a crew booked for Thursday, the twelfth, and I put in for a supervisor to call back by Friday the thirteenth.

A crew Thursday. Okay. Is it gonna be the same thing though? 'Cause that's what I'm sayin', it's wicked frustrating. We did this already. Somebody comes, says it's clear, and then the next rain it's comin' up again.

I'm going to add a note so it's not just a grate cleaning. Second backup at the same location, top was cleaned in January, still flooded. And I'll flag it for engineering, so it's not just the field guys deciding.

Okay. Engineering. That's, yeah, that's more like it. Because, honestly, I don't even use the basement, it's not my stuff down there, but Ileana's been dealing with this twice now and it's a lot. And they're gonna get another storm, it's March, it's gonna rain again.
It will. Can I get a good number for you? Luis gave me his, but if you're the one who's been tracking this I want the supervisor to have yours too.
Yeah, it's 401-555-0193. It's my cell.
401-555-0193. Got it. And you said tracking, is there anything you've been keeping?

Yeah, actually, that's the other thing. I been taking pictures. Every time. The drain backed up in January, the water in the basement, the crew there on the Friday, what it looked like after they left, then this weekend. All with the dates on 'em. I got like a whole log on my phone, kinda organized by day.
Oh, good. That's really useful. Hold onto those, don't send them anywhere yet. When the supervisor calls, tell them you have them and they'll tell you where they want them to go.
Okay, so send 'em now. Hang on, I'm pullin' 'em up, where do I send...
No, no, sorry, hold onto them. Don't send yet. Wait for the supervisor.
Oh. My bad. I heard 'send them.' [pause] Okay, I closed it. Hang onto 'em, wait for the call. Got it.
You're fine. I'm putting in the note that you have a dated photo log, so they know to ask.
Cool. And, um, is there like a claim form or somethin'? For the damage? Like if it's the city's drain and it's backing up into the house, twice, can Ileana put in for the freezer and all that?

There is a claims process with the city for property damage. It doesn't go through us here at Public Works though, it goes through City Hall. I can transfer you over to the clerk's office when we're done and they can tell you how to get the form.
Okay. Yeah, I'll probably have Ileana do it, it's her house, but I'll get the info.
That works. Your photos would help there too, by the way.
Yeah, that's kinda why I started takin' 'em. After the first time, I was like, nobody's gonna believe how bad it got. [crosstalk]
Sorry, go ahead.

No, I was just gonna say, I'm not tryin' to yell at you. I know it's not you. It's just, we called, we did what we were supposed to, somebody came, and then it happens again and it's worse. It's like, what was the point.

I understand. And you're not yelling. Okay, I've got it written up: repeat flooding at 688 Thames, two events this winter, January and this past weekend, first visit only cleaned the top, request for a senior person to look at it, flagged for engineering, supervisor to call you and Luis.
And Thursday the crew comes.
Thursday the crew comes. If nobody shows by end of day Thursday, call us back Friday morning and ask for me, Denise, and I'll chase it.
Okay. Thursday. I'll be around, I'll keep an eye out. I'll probably take pictures of that too, honestly.
Go right ahead. Want me to put you through to the clerk's office now for the claim form?
Yeah, sure, let's do it while I got you.
Alright, stay on the line, it'll ring a couple times. Thanks for calling, Doug.
Yeah, thanks Denise. Just, really, get somebody to look under there this time.
It's in the note. Transferring you now.
